questions.q: In the 6th edition of the Organon, §248 advises that the medicinal solution be:
opts: succussed a few times before each dose, so that each dose is slightly altered in potency
kept unshaken so that every dose has exactly the same potency
diluted 1:100 in fresh alcohol before each dose
questions.why: §248 directs that the bottle be given several succussions before each dose, so repeated doses are not identical and are better tolerated.

questions.q: A major limitation of card repertories is that they:
opts: need a computer to read the cards
ignore remedy grades, and one small card can wrongly exclude the true remedy
cannot be used for more than two rubrics
questions.why: Holes show only presence or absence, so grading is lost, and any card lacking the remedy eliminates it.

questions.q: The 'unsafe' (atticoantral) type of chronic suppurative otitis media is dangerous mainly because of:
opts: a central perforation of the pars tensa
questions.why: Cholesteatoma in the attic erodes bone and leads to intracranial and extracranial complications.

questions.q: Dysmenorrhoea in which the pains are relieved as soon as the menstrual flow begins is a keynote of:
questions.why: Lachesis is better once the discharge is established; in Cimicifuga the pain increases as the flow increases.

questions.q: Hahnemann's 'Chronic Diseases' second edition was published in five volumes between:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. The first edition appeared in 1828–1830.

questions.q: Kent traced the origin of psora to:
opts: disordered willing and thinking of man, a spiritual sickness that came before the itch
infection by the itch mite alone
questions.why: Kent (Lectures on Homoeopathic Philosophy) held psora to be the primitive disorder of the human race, arising from man's wrong willing and thinking.

questions.q: Renal colic, worse on the left, with pains radiating in all directions and bubbling sensations in the kidney, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Berberis: radiating pains, bubbling sensation.

questions.q: Profuse sweat on the head of a fat, flabby child is Calcarea carb. A child who is thin, emaciated about the neck, with a craving for salt and a map-like tongue, needs:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Nat mur: emaciation descending from the neck, mapped tongue.

questions.q: The mature cyst of Entamoeba histolytica contains:
questions.why: The mature infective cyst of E. histolytica is quadrinucleate; the cyst of the non-pathogenic E. coli has up to eight nuclei.

questions.q: The decimal scale of potentisation was introduced by:
questions.why: Hering introduced the decimal (1 in 10) scale. Hahnemann used the centesimal and, later, the LM scale.
